skill.name: constraint-driven-development
skill.description: Defines measurable project quality constraints and records them in CONSTRAINTS.md. Connects standards to checks, lifecycle stages, ratchets, exceptions, and diff-based guards against weakened quality gates.
skill.summary: Define measurable quality standards and guard them against regressions.
skill.author: addyosmani

security_audit.summary: All 87 static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, filename regular expressions, or a constrained git helper that avoids shell interpolation. The review found no prompt injection or malicious command intent. One medium-risk semantic issue remains because the floor guard can print matched source text without redaction.

remediation.issue: The floor guard logs matched diff text, which can expose sensitive values in local or CI output.
remediation.suggestion: Report only the rule and file location, or redact recognized secret formats before printing any source text.

semantic_findings.title: Matched Diff Content May Be Exposed in Logs
semantic_findings.description: The floor guard stores up to 120 characters from each matched diff line and prints that text to standard error. A matching line containing a credential or other sensitive value could therefore enter local or CI logs despite the stated redaction contract.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The reference directly retains matched source text and interpolates it into console output. No redaction step is applied before logging.

content.value_statement: Teams often lack measurable quality standards, allowing checks and thresholds to drift during development. This skill defines a shared contract and connects each constraint to practical enforcement.
actual_capabilities: Inspects project configuration, test tooling, coverage output, CI files, and agent guidance before asking questions.
Guides a four-question interview to select dimensions, enforcement levels, target numbers, and acceptable check duration.
Creates a CONSTRAINTS.md contract with measurable rules, commands, lifecycle stages, rationales, and tracked exceptions.
Recommends established tools for types, linting, coverage, security, performance, accessibility, architecture, and mutation testing.
Uses current measurements as ratchets when fixed thresholds would fail the existing project.
Provides a diff-scoped floor guard for suppressions, skipped tests, removed assertions, unfinished work, and weakened constraints.
limitations: The interview requires an interactive user when project-specific choices are unavailable.
Performance and accessibility checks require a running application URL.
The floor guard uses regular expressions and cannot detect deliberate or complex evasion.
Recommended tools may require installation, configuration, licensing review, or CI resources.

use_cases.title: Set Standards for a New Project
use_cases.description: Define measurable quality gates before implementation expands, with defaults tied to available tools and current project evidence.

use_cases.title: Protect an Autonomous Workflow
use_cases.description: Add fast checks and diff guards that detect weakened thresholds, silenced tools, skipped tests, and unfinished work.

use_cases.title: Stabilize Existing CI Gates
use_cases.description: Convert inconsistent checks into documented constraints with owners, commands, lifecycle stages, baselines, and explicit exception expiry dates.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Quality Contract
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this project and help me define a basic quality contract. Ask one question at a time and use measured defaults when I am unsure.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs practical standards for an existing repository.

prompt_templates.title: Define Measurable Gates
prompt_templates.prompt: Create project constraints for coverage, security, and linting. Measure the current baseline, explain each threshold, and identify the command that verifies it.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team knows which quality dimensions matter but needs enforceable numbers.

prompt_templates.title: Stage Checks by Cost
prompt_templates.prompt: Add quality gates for edit, task, review, and CI phases. Keep fast checks under five seconds and scope expensive checks to changed files.
prompt_templates.scenario: A mature project needs efficient checks across its development lifecycle.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Constraint Integrity
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit our constraints for weakened thresholds, new suppressions, skipped tests, removed assertions, unfinished stubs, and untracked exceptions. Propose remediations without lowering standards.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced team needs to detect attempts that make failing checks easier to pass.

output_examples.input: Set up constraints for a TypeScript web application with tests, preview deployments, and no documented quality gates.
output: Created a quality contract covering types, linting, secret scanning, changed-line coverage, accessibility, and performance.
Assigned fast checks to edit time, coverage to task completion, and browser checks to preview deployment.
Recorded current coverage as a ratchet and required owners and expiry dates for exceptions.

output_examples.input: Our legacy Python service has low coverage, so fixed coverage targets fail immediately.
output: Measured current project coverage and set it as a non-regression baseline.
Applied a stronger coverage target only to changed lines.
Placed type, lint, and secret checks in the fast stage while keeping broader security scans in CI.

output_examples.input: Review a branch where tests pass after several quality configuration changes.
output: Flagged a lowered threshold, a newly skipped test, and an added suppression for review.
Kept tightened constraints silent and requested tracked exceptions for approved deviations.
Recommended fixing the implementation instead of weakening the quality contract.

best_practices: Measure the current baseline before choosing thresholds that could leave the project permanently failing.
Place each check according to execution cost, and keep the edit loop focused on changed files.
Record every exception with a reason, owner, and expiry date.
anti_patterns: Do not lower a threshold or disable a checker merely to make a change pass.
Do not define a numeric constraint without naming the command that verifies it.
Do not rely only on tests written by the same system that produced the implementation.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates a project quality contract, usually in CONSTRAINTS.md, with measurable rules, verification commands, lifecycle stages, and exception handling.

faq.question: Does it require a new project?
faq.answer: No. It can measure an existing codebase and establish ratchets that prevent current quality metrics from declining.

faq.question: What happens when I do not know a target number?
faq.answer: The skill measures the current value, records it as a baseline, and prevents regression until the team chooses a stronger target.

faq.question: Will every check run after each edit?
faq.answer: No. Fast checks run near edits, while expensive coverage, browser, mutation, and security checks move to later stages.

faq.question: Can the floor guard replace code review?
faq.answer: No. It detects common diff patterns with regular expressions, but human review remains necessary for context, intent, and sophisticated changes.

faq.question: How are temporary exceptions handled?
faq.answer: Each exception should include a rule, path, reason, owner, and expiry date so deviations remain visible and accountable.
